title: Beyond the Efficiency-Efficacy Dilemma: A Critical Analysis of Transferability in Adversarial Malware Detection
abstract: arXiv:2611.33243v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Machine Learning (ML) models are already being deployed at scale for malware detection. Therefore there is a pressing need to rigorously study adversarial robustness. To that end, we introduce the Adversarial AI Engine (AAIE): a platform for automated security stress-testing. We performed transfer attacks, via EMBER2018, against a Random Forest target. Counterintuitively, we found single-step FGSM to have the highest attack success rate (ASR) of 52.9% compared to iterative PGD with 45.2% (p < 0.002). Compared to iterative attacks which tend to overfit surrogate networks creating brittle perturbations, FGSM created more transferable examples. We benchmarked our attacks using ASR, transferability score, evasion rate, and resilience index. Through these metrics, proposed in concordance with emerging standards in AI governance, we expose shortcomings as our transferability scores peak at ~0.8 with constrained perturbations. translated_title: 超越效率与效能的困境：对抗性恶意软件检测中可迁移性的批判性分析
translated_abstract: 机器学习模型已被大规模部署用于恶意软件检测，因此迫切需要对对抗鲁棒性进行严格研究。为此，我们引入了对抗人工智能引擎（AAIE）：一个自动化安全压力测试平台。我们通过EMBER2018数据集对随机森林目标模型实施了迁移攻击。与直觉相反，我们发现单步FGSM攻击具有最高的攻击成功率（ASR），达到52.9%，而迭代式PGD攻击为45.2%（p < 0.002）。与容易过拟合代理网络从而产生脆弱扰动的迭代攻击相比，FGSM生成了更具可迁移性的对抗样本。我们使用攻击成功率、可迁移性得分、逃逸率和韧性指数对攻击进行了基准测试。通过与新兴AI治理标准相一致的这些指标，我们暴露了现有方法的不足——在受限扰动条件下，可迁移性得分最高仅约为0.8。
tldr: 该论文提出对抗人工智能引擎（AAIE）自动化安全压力测试平台，揭示单步FGSM攻击在恶意软件检测迁移攻击中比迭代式PGD更有效（成功率52.9%对45.2%），并依据新兴AI治理标准提出了包含可迁移性得分、逃逸率和韧性指数的攻击评估指标体系。
